image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small-format Lotus's supermarket building, detailed front elevation with a glazed frontage and automatic sliding doors under a deep fascia carrying the green Lotus's wordmark on an illuminated sign panel, green and white composite cladding across the upper front and a flat entrance canopy with downlights, plain rendered side and rear walls with a roller service shutter, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: green and white composite cladding and printed illuminated sign face at the front, aluminium glazing and plate glass, flat painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Lotus's / CP Axtra, rebranded from Tesco Lotus. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 -- not a pass self-score. 1624/16000 triangles, 12/16 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 12/16 unique geometries. Materials are the tight axis, not draw calls: the facade grid buys 46 tones for one submission and one shader, and the two instanced systems the previous build spent on canopy plates and condensers were given back as merged components that read closer to the plate for the same cost.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7, and for the first time on this prop the envelope is CHECKED rather than asserted: the front homography (scratch/_retail/rect_lotus.py) is anchored on a base line fitted at y = 637.0 + 0.332 (x-120) and a coping-top line at y = 288.0 + 0.2154 (x-200), which are 375.6 px apart at plate x=200. Taking that as the declared 4.60 m gives 81.7 px/m, and the measured coping band is then 0.159 m against the 0.16 built and the green cladding's top edge falls at 4.44 -- both already in the model. Two packaged rooftop units break the side roofline.
featureReviews.notes: The independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate agrees on height within 2.5% and reads 11% deeper; the declared size is the kit's shared retail module across seven siblings, so the declaration wins and the proxy divergence is reported rather than followed. The grey coping run on the front parapet is what takes the model to exactly 4.60.

featureReviews.evidence: Signboard rebuilt to the rectified plate: white face X -1.65..+1.28 by Y 2.98..4.06, i.e. 2.93 x 1.08 m centred at X -0.19. The previous build had it centred on the building axis and 0.86 m tall. Green 'Lotus' (#0E7A4F) and a gold apostrophe-s (#E3A81C) measured off crops/fascia.png at PBR confidence 0.762, BAKED to a webp data URI and assigned as a post-construction canvas -- one material, one draw call, and the same mark on every machine. The canvas's plain field is GREEN, so the board's five other faces read as the green tray the plate shows around its white face.
featureReviews.notes: The glyphs are Liberation Sans Bold, a SUBSTITUTE for the brand's own rounded face, and the gold apostrophe is drawn as a teardrop because a font apostrophe is a straight tick. Both are recorded as substitutes rather than presented as the brand mark. Baking is what stopped the fit depending on headless Chrome's font fallback.

featureReviews.evidence: The facade is now a panel GRID in geometry, not a colour. Horizontal joints scanned in the rectified plate's x=+3.67 column land at Y 0.727, 1.46, 2.213, 2.967, 3.733 and 4.49 -- six courses of 0.748 m to within 0.02. Vertical joints along Y=4.43 land at X -3.56, -2.75, -1.99, -1.10, -0.17, 0.76, 1.64, 2.39 and 3.20 -- eight bays of 0.845 m between the outer two, with a 0.38 m return at the left edge and the 0.74 m pilaster at the right. A cell-by-cell classification (green where G-R > 12) gives the white field as course 3 across bays 1-8 and course 4 in bays 2 and 7 only, which is the stepped field flanking the sign. 46 boxes, one component, one draw call, two measured tones (#549070 and #E4E6E1) as a per-panel vertex colour on a WHITE material.
featureReviews.notes: Two corrections carried by this feature. The parapet RING is grey on this plate, not green: the previous build clad the whole ring and every upstand in the front's cladding colour. And the panel joints, which the previous build's own notes dismissed as 'below the resolution worth geometry', are the most legible thing on the elevation at a grazing angle -- they are built as a 0.025 m reveal onto the grey substrate behind.

featureReviews.evidence: Shopfront aligned to the panel grid at X -3.56..+2.36, sill 0.06 to head 2.42, centred at -0.60 like the canopy above it rather than on the building axis. SIX mullions run sill to head on one 0.07 m section (the InstancedMesh); the door opening spans -1.55..+0.65; ONE horizontal transom at Y 1.78 defines the door head and ONE short mullion stops at it. Tinted pane at measured #808582, opacity 0.92, recessed behind the framing, with the plate's green vinyl band across its full width at Y 0.98..1.12.
featureReviews.notes: Two things this feature had to be measured against rather than eyeballed. The transom was authored at 2.00 and was invisible: the canopy's front-bottom edge at (2.26, 3.44) occludes the facade plane below about 1.99 at the review elevation, so the door head the brief asks to SEE has to sit under that. And the vinyl band was authored at z 2.575, 0.03 m in front of the pane, where it did not survive the transparent pass at all; at 2.60..2.65 it renders. The plate shows shelving and floor markings through the glass and none of it is modelled -- this is an exterior shell, and the band is applied ON the glazing rather than read through it.

featureReviews.evidence: ONE continuous slab, x -3.60..+2.58, replacing six instanced plates on a 1.06 m pitch that read as a flight of steps. Its junction with the wall is a dark seam that column scans of the plate put at Y 2.54 in every column from x=180 to x=540 -- the previous build had the plates floating at 3.00. Deck z 2.64..3.44, back upstand, nose bead reaching the declared 3.50 face, recessed fascia downstand, and five light fittings standing ON the deck 0.34 m forward of the wall, at the 1.14 m spacing the rectified plate gives.
featureReviews.notes: The fittings are the correction that matters most here: the previous build merged a downlight into each plate's UNDERSIDE, where the plate plainly shows small chrome boxes on top. Their count and spacing are read off the rectified front at 0.75 confidence -- the apparent x positions are corrected for the 0.34 m the fittings stand forward of the facade plane.

featureReviews.evidence: 18 ribbed slats plus a head box on the +X wall, at measured-and-corrected #9AA0A6, with the corner pilaster's green return now wrapping onto the same elevation at x 3.80..3.96.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged from the previous build except for the pilaster return beside it. The albedo was lifted from the crop mean #71757B, which sits on the shaded elevation and rendered the shutter as a dark panel against a plate that shows light mill grey.

name: Lotus's Store Building
notes: Built on the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m building module: detailed front elevation, plain rendered side and rear walls, no loose objects outside. A real Lotus's is far larger; scaled down to the shared module, so it reads as a small-format store. Livery is the current green Lotus's branding, not the former blue and red Tesco Lotus.
